ak_arrowhead_wall.blurb: Arrowhead Wall is the upper tier of the Dew Mound cliff above the Eagle River valley, in the Chugach foothills east of Anchorage. It holds six lines, mostly bolted, with a single trad route. The grades sit in the 5.10 to 5.13 range, with most of the bolted climbs at 5.11 and above, so it suits strong climbers rather than beginners. It sits to the left of the main wall, so you reach it by continuing past the lower wall and picking up a steep, loose path through scree and brush. Expect a longer, more committed day than the lower wall.

ak_emperor_boulder.blurb: Emperor Boulder is one of three glacial erratic blocks at Black Rapids Bouldering in the Delta Range of interior Alaska, near the Richardson Highway. It has six problems spanning an unusually wide spread: an easy V1, a few mid-range problems around V3 to V6, and a couple of hard lines up to V8. The stone is described as solid, with grip somewhere between that of its two neighbouring boulders. A flagged path through the trees links it to the nearby boulders in a few minutes, and a couple of hard single-move lines are still unclimbed.

ak_denali.blurb: Denali is the highest summit in North America, rising to about 20,300 feet in the Alaska Range of Denali National Park. This is serious glaciated mountaineering, not a crag: the listed lines are snow and steep-snow climbs plus a few ice and mixed pitches at moderate to mid-range ice grades. The West Buttress is by far the busiest route, with trail markers and regular patrols, while the other lines see far fewer parties and demand more route-finding and self-reliance. Storms are frequent, April is quietest, and mid-May to early July is busiest. Climbers fly in or walk in from Talkeetna or Wonder Lake.
